topic: Tight hips and glutes: massage plus movement

slides.headline: Massage for tight hips: half the answer
slides.sub: Massage can ease the tension. Movement helps it last.

slides.title: Tight is often tired
slides.body: Hips and glutes that feel tight are often under-used, or stuck working in one position all day. The feeling is real, even when your range of movement looks normal.

slides.title: What massage can do
slides.body: Remedial massage around the glutes, hips and lower back can ease tension and help you move more comfortably for a while. It's a helpful short-term tool, not the whole plan.

slides.title: Three moves after your session
slides.body: Try glute bridges, a figure-four stretch and side-lying leg lifts. Ten slow reps or a 30-second hold each, once or twice a day, helps keep things moving.

slides.title: Break up the sitting
slides.body: Stand and walk for a minute or two every half hour. Hips like variety, so switch between sitting, standing and moving through the day, even on busy desk days.

slides.title: When to get it checked
slides.body: Groin pain, sharp catching or locking, pain that wakes you at night, or tingling down the leg is worth assessing with a physio or GP rather than massaging.

slides.headline: Ease it, then move it
slides.body: Our remedial massage therapists work on the tension and send you home with simple moves to keep it easing. Book online — link in bio.

caption:
Tight hips and glutes? A massage feels great. What you do next matters just as much.

That tight feeling often comes from muscles that are tired or stuck in one position for hours. Remedial massage can ease the tension and help you move more freely for a while, and that's the perfect window to add some movement.

Try glute bridges, a figure-four stretch and side-lying leg lifts once or twice a day, and get up from your desk every half hour. Groin pain, catching or tingling down the leg are worth getting assessed first.

story.headline: Tight hips after a desk day?
story.body: Ten glute bridges, a figure-four stretch and a two-minute walk. Repeat tomorrow.
